readings: For every constructor in the constructors table, count its constructorStandings records, including zero for constructors with none. Compute the average of those counts across all constructors. Show the 10 constructors with counts above that average and the largest differences, giving constructorId, nationality, record count, and count minus average. Order by difference descending, then constructorId ascending.

For each constructor with at least one constructorStandings record, count its standings records. Compute the average of those counts across constructors with at least one record. Show the 10 constructors with counts above that average and the largest differences, giving constructorId, nationality, record count, and count minus average. Order by difference descending, then constructorId ascending.
queries:
WITH counts AS (
    SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality,
           COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) AS record_count
    FROM constructors AS c
    LEFT JOIN constructorStandings AS cs
        ON cs.constructorId = c.constructorId
    GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality
),
average_count AS (
    SELECT AVG(record_count) AS avg_count
    FROM counts
)
SELECT constructorId, nationality, record_count,
       record_count - avg_count AS difference
FROM counts
CROSS JOIN average_count
WHERE record_count > avg_count
ORDER BY difference DESC, constructorId ASC
LIMIT 10

WITH counts AS (
  SELECT constructorId, COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM constructorStandings
  GROUP BY constructorId
),
average_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(record_count) AS avg_count
  FROM counts
)
SELECT c.constructorId,
       c.nationality,
       ct.record_count,
       ct.record_count - a.avg_count AS difference
FROM counts AS ct
JOIN constructors AS c ON c.constructorId = ct.constructorId
CROSS JOIN average_count AS a
WHERE ct.record_count > a.avg_count
ORDER BY difference DESC, c.constructorId ASC
LIMIT 10
